305 contributions

Familiar Vietnamese Flavors with an Elegant Touch
Jul 2026 • Solo
“Bánh Đập” Pâté — I liked that the rice cracker was crunchy, but not so hard that it took extra effort to bite into. The pâté was smooth and creamy without being overly fishy, while the scallion oil added freshness and aroma. Each bite was flavorful, and I thought the portion was just right.

Seafood Rice Noodle Roll — The rice noodle was silky, delicate, and incredibly soft, though a little slippery from the sauce. The seafood filling was flavorful, and the garnishes on top added color to the dish Overall, I would say this was an elevated take on bánh cuốn.

Local Grilled White Pomfret — The char on the pomfret was noticeable, and the skin was crispy without tasting burnt. The fish itself was fresh, moist, and tender, while the herbs were fresh and fragrant. I just wish there had been more sauce, as I didn’t think there was quite enough for the amount of fish and greens on the plate.

Young Rice Panna Cotta — The panna cotta was silky and delicate. It was tasty, with just the right amount of sweetness without being very sweet.

The service was excellent.

Best meal in Ho Chi Minh
Apr 2026 • Family
Super delicious food, a great wine list and reasonable prices. We ordered a mix of starters including chicken skewers, tuna tataki, spring rolls and garlic butter seafood. All were great and much better/different to what we expeyfeom the menu.

The same theme occurred with the mains. The fish dishes we chose and the beef were all exceptionally well executed but the chicken roulade was even better with delicious Vietnamese flavours coming through what is more often a European dish.

The wine list looked excellent but unfortunately they'd sold out of quite a lot of the nicer wines. We settled on an American cab sauv which we liked enough to go through 2 bottles between the 3 of us. 

If there's only one restaurant you get to in Ho Chi Minh, make it this one.

Excellent food, service, drinks, high quality
Mar 2026 • Friends
We had the 3 and 5 course fixe lunch special, actually we came here twice for this because it was so good. The second time we brought a group of my son’s friends who were only in town for the morning. This is a high quality restaurant and everything from the food to the drinks are great. The duck spring rolls are crispy & delicious and served elegantly in little baskets separated from the greens. The pepper elder salad has shrimp with a delicious blend of greens that was so good. The betel leaf wrap was unique and tasted great. The Bo Kho tart was good, but we wish it had more of the true Vietnamese Bo Kho flavor, but the crust was very nice. 

The drinks here are also excellent. We ordered a pot of jasmine tea and 2 glasses of ice. The tea was incredibly fragrant and the iced tea was so fresh because of the way it was prepared and served. The pear mocktail was delicate and delicious, as were the other mocktails served. They really do a fine job on their beverages too. 

For dessert they ran out of the mochi and were going to serve us a brownie, but we asked for a different substitute and they kindly gave us a dessert with coconut and ice cream instead, it was really good. 

We would like to come back here and try more of their menu, as the food, the beverages, the service all are top rate here.

reviews.review_text:
texasanthony
houston181 contributions
0
Bom is the bomb!
Oct 2024 • Couples
Been monitoring this restaurant for a couple of years now. Once it received a Michelin designation earlier this year, I knew I have to add it to my VN itinerary. Wasn't planning on dining on this particular evening, but our other Bib Gourmand plans ended badly and we were still somewhat hungry. We arrived a little underdressed for my taste but were warmly welcomed by the doorman nonetheless. No reservation, no problem. The setup and location - ideal. The foods - perfection. The service - impeccable. I got the Home Set fixed menu, a scaled down version of their Michelin Premium Set. Five courses starting with the spring salad followed by a whimiscal take on canh chua as a gazpacho. It was at this point that I suspect my journey might be taking a turn towards the unknown. Next was the Wagyu Pho Mini Burger. Ever had pho on a bun before? Well, I did and I don't mean that short-lived TexMex monstrosity that was the phorito. This was a refined dish of sliced seasoned waygu with pho accompaniments between a bun that's somehow infused with pho flavors. Not sure how the chef pulled it off but I'm glad he did. I can taste the fusion of East meets West that he's striving for. Next came the main course - chicken risotto. On the surface when I saw the name, I was prepared to be underwhelmed. However, the first bite of the risotto revealed something unexpected. A crunch! The mushy risotto was complimented by crunchy homini used in traditional xoi bap. The two consistencies matched perfectly with the flavoring from the seasoned mushrooms and fat drippings of the deliciously golden crisp roasted chicken. The roasted chicken was oh so, so good that I might never eat fried chicken again (lol, who I'm I kidding, the KFC colonel next door is already winking at me)! The fixed menu sweetly closed with a deliteful black sesame cream thingy called Me Den (my American friends should take care when pronouncing this. ). Overall this fixed menu was a great introduction to what Bom has to offer, but I'd be remissed not to mention the a la carte offerings that my wife partook. She got the Bom Set and a seasonal item that can only be described as an open-face bo la lot. Ok, just get the Bom Set, either as an a la carte or as part of a price fixed menu. Just do it. It's a combo appetizer dish that has items highlighting the chef's creativity towards achieving East-West balance. Every bite will have arriving at an epiphany of 'Wait, I've tasted this before, but hmm, not quite like this though'. Then there's the open-face bo la lot dish that I'm at a lost for words to describe (shocking, I know). It's like a flavor explosion, a cacophony of tastes, and a fireworks finale all rolling into your mouth at the same time. It's wow, just wow! I'm VN and a true lover of all things foods, as my waist line can attest. My wife is also VN and can cook like a motha. There's no hyperbole here when I say that this meal was THE BEST Vietnamese food experience we ever had too date, VN or worldwide! Very bold, I know. If these guys keep their creativity up and the service remains impeccable, there is no doubt they will get a Michelin star within a year or so. So fly, don't walk, over here now when the price is still affordable. You won't regret it.

You MUST visit here!
Nov 2023 • Solo
For my last day in Ho Chi Minh City I decided to search for a treat and this place seemed to tick the boxes. It looked nice, a good menu, and popular cocktails.

I predicted that I would have a nice meal, but ‘nice’ doesn’t do it anywhere near enough justice! This was a PHENOMENAL visit!

The staff are all incredibly kind and polite, and the bartender even managed to pull out a Frangelico Sour just for me (I never get these in bars!).

All of the food looked amazing and I wanted to taste as much as I could, so I went for one of the set menus which was 5 courses, and each one was just incredible.

The chef(s) have clearly put a lot of thought into each dish and the combinations work wonderfully, I didn’t want it to end. Every bite was delicious. 

And to top all of this off, it was remarkably well priced! For 5 courses and 2 cocktails I paid 1,300,000 - which equates to £40. If I had this in Europe, I would easily be paying 4x that amount!

I implore you to check this out! Both you and your tastebuds will thank me for it.

First and best meal, well worth the price tag
Dec 2022
We chanced upon this restaurant whilst roaming the city, slightly dazed and increasingly hungry after our flight in from Singapore. It's easy to miss BO'M and it's unassuming exterior, but the interior is impressive to say the least. We were quickly led past the bar, and up stairs, to the balcony area which overlooks the bustling streets of Ho Chi Minh. We're not big salad people, but we wolfed down the beet root salad quickly and did the same to each dish that was served. They do a delightful spin on Vietnamese essentials and this was a wonderful introduction to the gastronomical experience that awaited us during our stay. Having said that, the prices were steep for Vietnam, actually our most expensive meal for the trip, but despite this, 10/10, will recommend!
